## Problem

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a convex open set and let

$$
f\in C^1(\Omega).
$$

Prove that for any $x,y\in\Omega$, there exists a point

$$
\xi\in [x,y]
$$

such that

$$
f(y)-f(x)
=
\nabla f(\xi)\cdot (y-x).
$$

Here

$$
[x,y]
=
\{x+t(y-x):0\leq t\leq1\}
$$

denotes the line segment joining $x$ and $y$.

## Solution

If $x=y$, the conclusion is immediate. Thus assume that $x\neq y$.

Since $\Omega$ is convex,

$$
x+t(y-x)\in\Omega
$$

for every $t\in[0,1]$.

Define the one-dimensional function

$$
g:[0,1]\to\mathbb R
$$

by

$$
g(t)
=
f\bigl(x+t(y-x)\bigr).
$$

Since $f\in C^1(\Omega)$, we have

$$
g\in C^1([0,1]).
$$

By the ordinary one-dimensional Lagrange mean value theorem, there exists some

$$
t_0\in(0,1)
$$

such that

$$
g(1)-g(0)=g'(t_0).
$$

Now

$$
g(1)=f(y),
\qquad
g(0)=f(x).
$$

By the chain rule,

$$
g'(t)
=
\nabla f\bigl(x+t(y-x)\bigr)\cdot(y-x).
$$

Therefore,

$$
f(y)-f(x)
=
\nabla f\bigl(x+t_0(y-x)\bigr)\cdot(y-x).
$$

Set

$$
\xi=x+t_0(y-x).
$$

Then $\xi\in[x,y]$, and hence

$$
\boxed{
f(y)-f(x)
=
\nabla f(\xi)\cdot(y-x).
}
$$

This proves the multivariable Lagrange mean value theorem.

## Remark

The convexity assumption guarantees that the entire line segment joining $x$ and $y$ remains inside $\Omega$. This allows the multidimensional problem to be reduced directly to the one-dimensional mean value theorem.

As an immediate consequence,

$$
|f(y)-f(x)|
\leq
\sup_{z\in[x,y]}|\nabla f(z)|\,|x-y|.
$$

In particular, if $\Omega$ is convex and

$$
\|\nabla f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}<\infty,
$$

then

$$
|f(y)-f(x)|
\leq
\|\nabla f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}|x-y|,
$$

so $f$ is Lipschitz continuous on $\Omega$.
